BiblicalUsage: The word means to compel, to constrain: the lord tells his servant to go out into the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, that his house may be filled — and Paul asks Peter, before them all, why he compels the Gentiles to live as the Jews. The same word is the urgency of the invitation and the pressure of a false demand, and the difference is everything.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for compelling carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the difference — compel them to come in to the feast, but do not compel Gentiles to live as Jews.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
